lessons.title: Writing a clear topic sentence
lessons.description: Introduce one main idea so a reader can predict what the paragraph explains.
lessons.content: A paragraph develops one main idea. A topic sentence tells the reader that idea, while the other sentences explain it with details or examples. A focused topic sentence is neither too broad nor a list of unrelated points.
learning_objectives: Identify the main idea of a short paragraph.
Write a focused topic sentence for a familiar subject.
prerequisites: Write complete sentences and identify a paragraph topic.

explanation_sections.title: Main idea and supporting details
explanation_sections.body: Read all the details and ask what they have in common. A paragraph about saving water might mention closing taps, reporting leaks and reusing clean water for plants. These details support the main idea that small actions conserve water.

explanation_sections.title: Make the sentence focused
explanation_sections.body: A useful topic sentence names the subject and says something about it. 'School gardens help learners' is focused; 'Gardens' is too broad. Recap: choose one main idea, state it clearly, and make sure each supporting sentence belongs to it.

worked_examples.prompt: Details: learners borrow storybooks, practise reading and discuss new words. Write a topic sentence.
worked_examples.solution: The school library helps learners develop reading skills.
worked_examples.reasoning: The sentence groups borrowing, reading practice and vocabulary discussion under one central benefit.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: Which sentence best introduces a paragraph about keeping a classroom tidy?
options: A tidy classroom makes it easier to learn.
questions.correct_answer: A tidy classroom makes it easier to learn.
questions.explanation: It states a central idea that relevant details can support.

questions.prompt: A paragraph explains how a school garden supports learning. Which detail fits best?
options: The football has a blue stripe.
A bus stopped near the market.
questions.explanation: Observing plant growth directly supports learning through a school garden.

questions.prompt: What should a writer check after choosing a topic sentence?
options: That each supporting detail relates to its main idea.
That the paragraph changes topic in every sentence.
That every sentence is a question.
That the details are placed in alphabetical order.
questions.correct_answer: That each supporting detail relates to its main idea.
questions.explanation: Relevant details keep a paragraph focused and coherent.

lessons.title: Choosing supporting details
lessons.description: Select facts, reasons and examples that explain a paragraph's main idea.
lessons.content: Supporting details make a main idea clearer. A writer can use a reason, a fact from a text, or a specific example. Each detail should answer a reader's question about the topic sentence rather than introducing a new subject.
learning_objectives: Distinguish a relevant detail from an unrelated one.
Add an example that explains a main idea.

explanation_sections.title: Test relevance
explanation_sections.body: Ask, 'Does this detail explain or prove the main idea?' If the topic is safe walking to school, wearing a visible reflector is relevant; a favourite meal is not. A detail can be true and still be unrelated.

explanation_sections.title: Use a specific example
explanation_sections.body: Specific details help readers picture an idea. Instead of 'exercise is useful', explain that walking, running or playing a game makes the body move. Recap: keep details true, clear and connected to the topic sentence.

worked_examples.prompt: Topic sentence: 'Planning helps learners finish assignments.' Add one supporting detail.
worked_examples.solution: A written plan can divide a large assignment into smaller tasks with dates for completing them.
worked_examples.reasoning: The detail explains how planning supports timely completion.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: Topic: ways to keep drinking water clean. Which detail is relevant?
options: Store it in a clean, covered container.
questions.correct_answer: Store it in a clean, covered container.
questions.explanation: A clean covered container relates directly to protecting drinking water.

questions.prompt: Why include an example in a paragraph?
options: It makes an idea more specific and easier to understand.
It removes the paragraph's main idea.
It changes every fact into an opinion.
It makes the reader guess the topic.
questions.correct_answer: It makes an idea more specific and easier to understand.
questions.explanation: An example shows what a general idea can look like in practice.

questions.prompt: A paragraph is about saving electricity at home. Which sentence is least relevant?
options: Switch off lights when leaving an empty room.
Use daylight when it is bright enough.
Unplug a charger when it is not being used.
questions.explanation: The sentence about drawing does not explain saving electricity.

lessons.title: Connecting ideas in a paragraph
lessons.description: Use simple linking words to show addition, contrast and result.
lessons.content: Linking words show how ideas relate. Words such as 'also' add information, 'but' signals contrast, and 'so' can introduce a result. Choose a link that matches the meaning rather than repeating one word in every sentence.
learning_objectives: Recognise addition, contrast and result relationships.
Choose a linking word that fits two connected ideas.

explanation_sections.title: Match word to relationship
explanation_sections.body: 'Also' adds a similar point: 'The path is short. It is also safe.' 'But' signals a difference: 'The bag is small, but it holds many books.' 'So' can connect a cause and result.

explanation_sections.title: Read the whole sentence
explanation_sections.body: Read both ideas and decide whether the second adds, differs or follows from the first. Recap: choose a linking word for meaning, then read the sentence aloud to check that it sounds logical.

worked_examples.prompt: Complete: 'It rained heavily, ____ the match was postponed.'
worked_examples.reasoning: The postponement is the result of the heavy rain.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: Choose a word that adds another similar point: 'We planted beans. We ____ planted spinach.'
questions.explanation: 'Also' adds another action to the first sentence.

questions.prompt: Complete the contrast: 'The walk was long, ____ the view was beautiful.'
Complete the result: 'Amina practised every day, ____ she became more confident.'
questions.explanation: 'So' introduces the result of practising every day.
